provisionalNotice: PROVISIONAL (pre-freeze). Not an offer, qualification or gate result; nothing here enables a cell, selects an allowance or changes a default.
note: The profile is wall-clock time of one instrumented native request: an attribution run, not a timing run. Finder and apply times include the cost of their own timers (estimated in overhead.json).

registry.note: the nine finders of IG-S03's implemented scopes (singles and the six naked/hidden pair, triple and quad finders) against every other registered finder of this source; variant-scoped finders (cage, inequality) run only on their variants

summary.reading: A ratio above 1 is the cost of the instrumentation plus whatever else differs between the two runs. The same-command arms differ only by the instrumentation and the run order; the time-separated comparators also differ by machine state, so a ratio within a few percent of 1 is not resolved against that noise. The instrumented wall time is never a before/after figure.

referenceCompatibility.statement: The accounting and loading path (host.cjs, loader.cjs, common.cjs, records.cjs, manifest.cjs) is byte-identical to the harness of IG-S02's generation evidence; the comparators are therefore compatible, with the changed files listed per row.

limits: The phase A wall of a frontier sample contains every floor test AND the DFS uniqueness checks that follow a stuck test; the per-purpose counts (floor, dfs, allowed/canonical, deepen) are counts of logical checks and DFS entries, not per-purpose or per-finder wall measurements.

Native-request finder shares (finder-profile.json) cannot be transplanted into frontier phase A, and they say nothing about the cost of a scoped cache. A per-finder profile of frontier phase A would be separately authorised work.

Classic9's empty frontier (every refused group proves ambiguous), the larger boards' above-band or shallow candidates and the budget-ended searches are different outcomes of different mechanisms, never interchangeable failures.

No frontier run was made for IG-S07: these are the IG-S05 screen trials as recorded (two samples of two grids per cell and mode at most, eight clusters per cell; zero verified hits in every mode) and, as a second dataset, the IG-S04 pilot trials (grid seeds 11 and 12, one sample each).

acceptance.evidence: every number is a measured wall time or a counted operation of the twelve fixed requests; no loose-count solve model is used
local-continuation time (context local) is its own row and share; a cohort's request-group time is not substituted for it; per-attempt cap reasons are listed from the engine's own work
the headline timings stay IG-S02's: profiled wall times appear only in the overhead and attribution tables, labelled instrumented

9 profiles reconcile (booked cells = root, residual in the rows); finder time is one number per finder and the stage cells hold the rest of the solver, never summed twice; profile consistency problems: 0

canonical ratings (difficulty.rate calls, equal to the engine's work counter), oracle solves (solves outside a rating), DFS entries/checks/backtracks and finder/loop budget checks are separate counters
9 of 9 profiled outputs equal their comparator in every digest section; hook restoration is checked in every request and in the engine checks
the hooks call no solve, draw no number and charge no budget; the engine checks compare the number of budget checks of an unpatched, a patched-without-runtime and a profiled run
every record carries source/case/trace metadata (trace off), the transform hashes, the calibration and its comparator; overhead.json holds the ratios

limitations: n = 1 profiled request per cell: shares are observations of one seed, not distributions; the per-kind rows are the samples of that request.

Wall-clock attribution inside one worker: process CPU is read once at the host (cpuTotal in overhead.json); no per-call CPU is taken. Process CPU also counts background threads (the Greater-Than cells show CPU/ready ratios above 1, as IG-S02's native Greater-Than runs did), so it is a side figure and never an attribution base.
DFS checks are the budget checks of the search loop; checks issued inside constraint propagation are not counted separately (UNIQUE_NODES units are larger).
The loop-check counter is derived (one check per pass plus one before a stuck result) and was checked against the budget's own count on a fake of the engine pieces only.
No frontier run was made: phase A is read from the IG-S05 ledgers; per-finder profiles of the frontier are not measured.
Killer and Greater-Than strategies (structure search, sign dig) run inside the dig and extra-structure steps through the same primitives; their own stages are not labelled separately.

sampleVsLocal.note: sample = ordinary + proposal samples; local = the local-continuation sample of an attempt (its dig, rating and tune steps included); other = setup and the full grids, extra structure and restart loop. Request-group time of a cohort is not this.

counters.note: canonical ratings = difficulty.rate calls (equal to the engine's own work ratings); oracle solves = logical solves that are not inside a rating; DFS entries/checks/backtracks are separate counters; DFS checks are the checks of the search loop only (checks inside constraint propagation are not counted)

bound.note: Ceilings, not forecasts: each removes the named wall time completely at zero cost from this profiled run (finder time includes its timers). A negative scan (a call that found nothing) is the only time a scoped cache can skip; how much of it a cache could skip depends on invalidation rates that this profile does not measure.
